mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which signals economic slowdown and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth for two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods with declining GDP, or the correlation between GDP decline and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, which boosts economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% in a month, coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000, signals a strengthening labor market and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases > 0.3% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts by more than 10% in a month, combined with a decrease in retail sales by more than 1%, signals a weakening consumer demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases > 10% and RSAFS decreases > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index by more than 0.5% per month for three consecutive months signals inflationary pressures, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate monetary tightening.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 300,000 in a month, without a corresponding increase in the unemployment rate, signals a strong labor market and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 300,000 in 1 month without UNRATE increase
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS increase without UNRATE increase on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
